lead: you are sure about a person from across a room, before either of you speaks, and the sureness does not wear off. what a stranger gets of you in that minute is a warm exterior with people already inside.
sun: the cover goes up around whoever the read approved, and it goes up that week — no waiting period, no test, nothing anybody had to pass. a man three months into knowing you has a key and a version of your life that stops at the door of whatever is holding it up. every person you have taken in is standing inside something whose one support has never been shown to any of them.
moon: the reading takes a minute and then it sets. a pause before an answer, the way somebody handles the woman clearing the table — that is the whole of the evidence, it is enough, and nothing done afterwards loosens it. so one stranger is admitted on a minute's work and another is declined on the same minute, and neither of them will ever be told which one happened.
pull: you read a stranger to the bone in ninety seconds and then hand them somewhere to stay. they read you in the same ninety seconds and see a warm room with plenty in it.
tension: the ones you shut the door on never find out there was a door. they leave with a verdict of their own, formed in the same evening yours was, and neither verdict takes an appeal. what everyone else carries away is drawn off the cover — easy, comfortable in some way nobody checks, a person with room to spare — and it never gets revised, because nothing further is ever issued.
cost: a stranger in trouble is under your arrangement the week you meet, ahead of people you have known a decade, and the read holds up often enough that nobody has made you defend it. the same speed runs in the other direction and never releases: whoever you got wrong in that first minute has no route to a second one, and never learns there was one.

lead: nine people have gone six years without meeting a board, a budget round, or a bad quarter of yours. your seat was carved before you were near it, and you have been spending it on them since.
sun: what you put up over them is made out of standing you did not accumulate. the complaint gets absorbed at your desk, the decision goes out signed as yours, the review is answered before anybody under you hears there was a review. the arrangement works because the room believes the shelter belongs to the institution. it belongs to one person's position inside the institution, and that is the item kept out of view.
moon: the carriage was on before you entered and it takes no instruction from you, so what the room reads every morning is somebody with no private question about the chair. that reading is the material the cover is made of. say out loud that the seat was granted and can be ungranted, and you have not confided in a colleague. you have taken the roof off nine desks.
pull: the room stays dry because you do not flinch in it. half of what you are covering them from is the fact that a chair carved for somebody else can be reassigned.
tension: the analyst who joined two years ago has you filed as somebody the firm was handed, who has never had a hard week, and he says so at the pub with some confidence, having watched you take three of them without a flicker. the correction is available in one sentence, and the sentence removes nine people's cover, so it stays unsaid and the file stands. every year of holding steady makes the file more plausible.
cost: nine careers have grown in a stretch of an institution where the weather does not land, and what comes out of that stretch is better than anything else in the building. all of it is fixed to one seat, held by one person who did not build it. the day the seat is reassigned, the cover comes down in a single piece, and the room will call it a reorganisation.

lead: people help themselves to you, and nobody asks first. a thing that size is taken to be the whole of what is there, so it occurs to nobody that a covered part exists.
sun: the covered ground is not large. one set of items — what a year actually costs you, who you owe, the thing you are frightened of — and it has never been opened to anybody, not by a policy you set but because a covering is what it is. the support under it is single, and whoever keeps that support upright spends every day of it being looked at.
moon: how much of you registers in a room was fixed before you had a view on it, and no week of yours has ever lowered it. fold this road in half and your sun comes down exactly on your moon — the covering at one end of the fold, the spread at the other, and no midpoint you could stand at to show part of it.
pull: everybody is certain they have the whole of you, because there is so much of you in the room. what nobody has seen is the part the rest of it is standing on.
tension: people who have known you fifteen years will tell a stranger there is nothing you do not say, and they are reporting what is in evidence. so requests arrive with no preliminary, and no signal you could send would come out small enough to mean that this month is a poor one for it. when something under the cover gives, the surprise is sized to match you, and the ones closest to it will say they had no idea, truthfully.
cost: put you in a new room and something in it loosens inside the minute, and whoever needed a large easy person to stand beside gets one without having to ask. the bad year arrives with no scale on it. what shows has always been the wrong end of you, and the rest opens for nobody, so the largest thing in the room goes through it unaccompanied.

lead: when you are finished with something it is finished the same fortnight, with no long dying middle. the eleven-year arrangement you shut in the spring had four people living under it, and the spring reached them as a single afternoon.
sun: you build the thing and then live inside it with the decision already in you. the household, the payroll, the room on a thursday — it is real cover, and people are genuinely dry under it. what is not available for inspection is the state of the support, so a year in which it has been failing looks, from underneath, exactly like the year it worked.
moon: when the turn comes it does not taper. nothing is wound down by degrees, nothing left running at a third of its size while people grow used to the idea. the whole of it goes inside a fortnight, and what remains in you afterwards is close to nil. so the structure gives no warning, the ending gives no gradient, and the people underneath get both at once.
pull: they get one afternoon where there should have been a year of signs. you had the year of signs. it sat under the part of the arrangement they were never shown.
tension: the account that forms afterwards is that you can end anything, and it gets repeated by people who were there and by people who only heard. what nobody outside can put a size to is the eighteen months you spent deciding, which would have been the warning, had the arrangement been able to show its own condition to the people standing in it. cold is the word that survives, and it survives because the alternative account cannot be produced.
cost: you can close a thing completely, with no remnant of it running on a fraction of itself, which is why nothing around you has ever spent four years visibly dying. people get the whole of an arrangement for as long as it exists. the closing reaches everyone else as weather, on a day of your choosing nobody else knew was a day, and years of goodwill go in one afternoon.
